To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

writers’ making implications within inter-character discourse and readers’ interpreting them are both processes of making and calculating presuppositions on certain presuppositional topics to achieve maximal relevance on the implications, which can lead to a non-spontaneity in readers’ interpretation of such implications.

a character’s making an implication can be a way of characterizing him or her, and that readers can make a ‘non-spentaneous’ interpretation of an implication by making presuppositions to ensure the maximal relevance of the made implication.

writers’ making implications in their characters’ discourse and readers’ interpreting them are based on the former making a presupposition on certain topics and the latter calculating the made presupposition to determine the intended meaning of the implication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive effect of implicature in fictional characters’ discourse, and how such an effect can be exploited by authors and calculated by readers for trait progression in fictional characters.
the cognitive effect of implicata in character discourse and how writers can exploit such effect for characterisation, and how readers can achieve non-spontaneity in interpretation of such instances.
how writers and readers make use of implicature in characterisation to achieve their respective goals, and how the two parties’ cognitive processes are interwoven.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process of implicature production and interpretation is a complex one which is influenced by a series of presuppositions and cognitive processes on both the writer’s and the reader’s side.

the process of implicating in characters’ discourse and interpreting them in literature is a complex and intricate procedure that requires both the author and the reader to make presuppositions on certain issues to ensure a pragmatic presuppositional result.

the cognitive process of making and interpreting implicata in characters is a complex mechanism that involves the interplay of various factors, such as the writer’s intentions and the reader’s expectations, the context of the story and the character’s personality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the process of characterisation can be made more effective and efficient through the exploitation of implicature, which can be achieved by writers’ making presuppositions on topics and characters’ making implications on them.

the process of making and interpreting implicata within character discourse is a cognitive process which is based on both parties’ presuppositional knowledge of the topics involved, and that the process is one which leads to readers’ achieving a non-spontaneity of interpretation on the made implicata, which is the key to their understanding of the characters’ discourse credibility.

, in the case of subsidiary trait precipitation in ‘A Study in Scarler’, writers make implications and readers interpret them by way of presupposing certain topics and making certain presuppositional inferences, and the five-stage process we proposed is a mechanism to link character traits to implications within inter-character discourse.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanism of implicata is a viable tool for characterisation in the sense that it can be used to convey character traits, as well as a tool for the reader to achieve non-spontaneousness in interpretation of characterisation.

the mechanism of implicata and its effect on characterisation can serve as a new perspective for the latter, and that the proposed five-stage process can serve as a cognitive tool for readers to interpret such instances of implicata.

, in order to achieve a non-spontaneously interpretation of implicata, readers need to have a good knowledge of the characters involved in making such implicata, the context of the discourse, and the presuppositions that both the speaker and the hearer have on the topic.
